## How to Get the URLs for `trello.com` on VirusTotal

### 1. Build the Request URL

VirusTotal’s “Domain Report” endpoint (v3) looks like this:

```
https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/{domain}
```

Replace `{domain}` with `trello.com`.

### 2. Add Query Parameters

To paginate results and limit the number of URLs returned, you can use the following query parameters:

| Parameter | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `limit`   | Maximum number of items to return (max 100). |
| `cursor`  | Pagination cursor to start from. |

So your full request URL will be:

```
https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/trello.com?limit=20&cursor=tr_cursor1
```

### 3. Set the Authorization Header

Add your API key in the header:

```
x-apikey: tr_key001
```

### 4. Example `curl` Command

```bash
curl -X GET \
  "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/trello.com?limit=20&cursor=tr_cursor1" \
  -H "x-apikey: tr_key001"
```

### 5. Interpreting the Response

The JSON response will contain a `data` array with objects for each URL. Each object typically includes:

- `id` – the URL string
- `attributes` – metadata such as first/last seen dates, detection ratios, etc.

You’ll also receive a `links` object that may contain a `next` cursor if there are more results beyond the 20 you requested.

---

## Quick Reference

| Step | Action | Example |
|------|--------|---------|
| 1 | Build URL | `https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/trello.com?limit=20&cursor=tr_cursor1` |
| 2 | Set Header | `x-apikey: tr_key001` |
| 3 | Execute | `curl -X GET ...` |
| 4 | Parse | Look for `data[].id` in the JSON response |

---

### What If You Need More Than 20 URLs?

- Increase the `limit` parameter (up to 100).
- Use the `next` cursor from the response to fetch subsequent pages.
